tasks.short: Observe training sessions, advise coaches and physical therapists on exercises and dangerous practices, record the advice in the athlete plan, and answer coaches' questions.

steps.what: Sports physician observes training sessions for potentially dangerous practices
Sports physician advises coaches and physical therapists on the proper use of exercises
Sports physician writes the advice in notes for each coach
Sports physician answers coaches' questions by phone

tasks.design: Advice is recorded once in each athlete's plan in the club's athlete management app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with exercise restrictions as fixed fields, which coaches and therapists can see, so the physician does not write separate notes per coach. Observing, advising and answering questions stay with the physician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Advice was written in separate notes for each coach.
tasks.enabler_now: Athlete management apps hold shared plans with restriction fields.
tasks.still_hard: Coaches outside the club do not use the app.
tasks.human_edge: Stopping a coach from pushing an injured athlete too soon.

reach.learn: Whether restrictions are visible to them.

evidence.claim: Athlete management apps can hold shared plans with restriction fields.
Health data are special category data; coaches see restrictions, not diagnoses.

assumptions: Boundary: from the training session to questions answered; training plans are outside.
Input contract: athletes consent to sharing restrictions; fallback is separate notes.
research_questions: Do coaches follow restrictions more often?

incremental.description: Sports physician asks athletes' consent for sharing restrictions.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small club; high: a large club with many coaches.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Search for courses and literature, attend courses and conferences, read literature, and record accreditation points.

steps.what: Sports physician searches for continuing education courses and new literature
Sports physician participates in continuing education courses and conferences
Sports physician reads literature to maintain knowledge and skills
Sports physician records accreditation points by uploading certificates

tasks.design: Saved searches and the professional association's course alerts arrive in one reading list ({OTHER}), so courses and literature are not searched for one by one. Accredited course providers register attendance points in the accreditation registry directly, so the physician uploads certificates only for courses abroad. Attending courses and reading stay with the physician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Courses were searched site by site and certificates uploaded by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Course providers register points directly; alerts gather sources.
tasks.human_edge: Learning a new technique hands-on from peers.

evidence.claim: Accredited course providers can register attendance points directly in accreditation registries.

assumptions: Boundary: from the learning need to points recorded; reregistration decisions are outside.
Input contract: providers register points; fallback is uploading certificates.
Courses and reading do not change.

incremental.description: Sports physician checks points registered by providers.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many courses abroad; high: mostly accredited local courses.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess the athlete's progress at check-ups, set the next rehabilitation phase and return-to-play criteria, read therapist and trainer reports, and write the progress note.

steps.what: Sports physician assesses injured athletes' progress at check-ups
Sports physician reads physiotherapist and trainer reports from e-mails
Sports physician supervises the rehabilitation by setting the next phase and return-to-play criteria
Sports physician writes the progress note with test results

tasks.design: Physiotherapists and trainers record progress scores (strength, range of motion, load tests) in the shared athlete record ({OPS_SYSTEM}), which shows them as a timeline, so the physician does not read separate e-mail reports. The progress note template fills those test results, and the physician adds the assessment and next phase. Assessing progress and setting return-to-play criteria stay with the physician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports came by e-mail and test results were copied into notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared athlete records show progress scores over time.
tasks.still_hard: Therapists outside the club report by e-mail.
tasks.human_edge: Judging when an athlete is mentally ready to play again.

reach.learn: Whether phases and criteria are clear.

evidence.claim: Shared athlete records can show progress scores from several disciplines over time.
Health data are special category data; sharing needs the athlete's consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the check-up due to the note written; therapy sessions are outside.
Input contract: therapists record scores in the shared record; fallback is e-mail.
Therapists enter scores in about the time an e-mail report took.
Return-to-play decisions stay with the physician.
research_questions: Do re-injuries after return to play fall?

incremental.description: Sports physician adds reports from outside therapists.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few athletes with outside therapists; high: a club team using the shared record.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess the athlete's needs, choose the orthotic or device with the therapist, fill the device application, check it, send it to the insurer, and write the order for the orthotist.

steps.what: Sports physician assesses the athlete's need for orthotics or adaptive equipment
Sports physician prescribes orthotics and adaptive equipment with the therapist
Sports physician fills the device application with medical justification
Sports physician checks the final application
Sports physician sends the application to the insurer by post or e-mail
Sports physician writes the device order for the orthotist

tasks.design: Device application forms in the record ({OTHER}) fill diagnosis, test results and earlier devices from the record, so the physician writes only the justification. Once checked, the application goes to the insurer through its electronic channel. The order for the orthotist uses a template per device type. Assessing needs and choosing the device stay with the physician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Applications were filled by hand with data copied from the record and sent by post.
tasks.enabler_now: Records prefill forms from structured data; insurers take electronic requests.
tasks.still_hard: Each insurer has its own form.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the brace that lets a runner train safely.
tasks.altitude: The physician justifies instead of copying data.

evidence.claim: Records can prefill application forms from structured data such as diagnoses and test results.
Health data are special category data; sharing with insurers needs a legal basis.

assumptions: Boundary: from the injury found to the order written; fitting is outside.
Input contract: forms set up per insurer; fallback is paper.
Insurers handle electronic applications as they did paper.
research_questions: Do insurers ask for more information less often?

incremental.description: Sports physician reports form changes to the record team.

approvals.approved_version: The application as checked by the physician in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: unusual devices; high: common insoles and braces with standard forms.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The sports physician keeps observing training, advising, assessing athletes and choosing devices; separate notes, e-mailed reports, copied results and hand-filled forms shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A physician with more time on the field.
